title: Nine Seconds of Air
subtitle: 呼吸与气息 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 呼吸与气息（生活与学习·健康医疗）
meta: 主题语境：呼吸与气息（生活与学习·健康医疗）　|　核心词汇：breath　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 breath 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 my mother was sent to count ① a breath she could not hold, and she said the holding was the whole of the lesson. The ② breath, meaning the air and not the life, was nine seconds long and was taken by whoever came last; a breath, she said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ breath in that ward had the same sound, and the ④ breath at the end, meaning the one the nurse counted and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever timed properly. A breath, my grandmother said, is nine parts air and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the air is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ breath was the whole of the life, meaning the life it carried and not the air. The ⑥ breath, meaning the life and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody watches and nobody questions; a breath, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both an air and a life. She said the life is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ breath had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the air. The ⑧ breath of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine seconds and eleven years of counting; a breath, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ breath I remember is the one at the end, which was timed in 1975 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ breath, my grandmother said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being counted; every breath, she said, is a life that has agreed to look like an air. She said the life was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 呼吸（指那口气本身，与生命相对）
C. 固定搭配：count a breath 数一次呼吸
D. n. 呼吸（指病房里每一次）
E. n. 呼吸（指末尾那一次）
F. n. 一口气；生命（抽象：与那口气相对）
G. n. 那份生命（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a breath she could not hold
The breath, meaning the air and not the life
breath was the whole of the life
the breath had become a number in a report
The breath of the whole thing
A breath, my grandmother said in 1978

answers.why: count a breath 意为“数一次呼吸”，1956 年母亲被派去数一次她屏不住的呼吸。
breath 意为“呼吸、气息”，指那口气本身而不是生命，长九秒，由最后走的人吸进。
breath 指病房里每一次呼吸，每一次都是同样的声音。
breath 指末尾那一次（护士数的那一次），是唯一有人认真计时的。
breath 意为“一口气、生命”，与那口气相对，父亲说 breath 就是那条命的全部。
breath 为抽象用法，指那份生命本身，是屋子里人人都守着看、却没人质疑的东西。
breath 意为“呼吸、气息”，到 1970 年这口气成了报告里的一个数字。
breath 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九秒和十一年的计数。
breath 意为“呼吸”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1975 年被计时，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
breath 为抽象总称，祖母说一口气是唯一会因为被认真数过而变好的东西。
